articles.headline: Rockets-Spurs: Thompson Block & Sengun Buckets Put Houston Back In Business
keyFacts: The Houston Rockets defeated the San Antonio Spurs 114-110 on Friday night.
Amen Thompson sealed the victory by blocking Victor Wembanyama's final shot attempt.
The Rockets will play their first back-to-back game of the season on Saturday against the Atlanta Hawks.
body: Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks the final shot attempt by San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) at the end of the game at Moody Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Houston Rockets sent a message with their Friday night 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs. The Rockets had already won their season opener on Wednesday. But in a sign of how far expectations had fallen for Houston this season, that matchup was against the lowly Dallas Mavericks. Just two games in, expectations are already on the rise.
Rockets-Spurs Was the Rockets’ First Real Test

Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets center Alperen Sengun (28) and teammates react after Sengun scored while drawing a foul during the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Moody Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs were a team that looked like they had Houston’s number last season. They had a lot of teams’ number, hence winding up as the second-last team standing, making it all the way to the NBA Finals.
In particular, though, the Rockets looked like they had an Amen Thompson problem in Thompson’s matchup with Wembanyama .

That matchup looked less problematic for the Rockets on Friday night, as the signature moment of it was Thompson swatting Wembanyama’s last-second shot attempt to tie. The block, which was on a post-up with Thompson as Wembanyama’s primary defender, sealed the game for Houston.
Thompson also scored 20 points on 9-of-15 shooting, pulled in 10 rebounds, and added four assists and two steals to go with his two blocks. He even made 1-of-2 three-pointers.
Caveats to Thompson’s Great Night

There are some caveats to Thompson’s revenge game versus the Spurs, though. For one thing, Thompson was the only Rockets starter with a negative plus/minus. In 36 minutes of playtime, the Rockets were outscored by 12 points.
That’s despite the Spurs declining to deploy their “secret” weapon against him. Wembanyama spent most of the game defending Alperen Şengün , rather than Thompson.

Finally, Wembanyama is off to a bumpy start to 2026-27 in general. The seven-foot-“four” Frenchman went 9-of-21 from the field against the Rockets, which was a major improvement on the 1-of-13 he managed in the Spurs’ opener.

Wembanyama’s impact is never limited to just his scoring. He has eight blocks already, two games into the season. But he didn’t seem quite prepared for just how hard opponents were going to lock in on shutting down his offense in 2026-27. The Spurs offense isn’t quite in Finals form just yet.
Why Houston’s Offense Looks Better
None of that should be overly concerning to Rockets fans. Right now, the team is healthy and firing on all cylinders.

Fred VanVleet ‘s return has made the Rockets’ offense look actually functional. His 14 points on 4-of-10 shooting to go with five assists against the Spurs undersells the impact he’s already having compared with his absence last season.

Şengün led all scorers in the game with 29 points on 10-of-20 shooting from the floor against the best defender in the NBA. He even went 4-of-6 in the fourth quarter, bamboozling San Antonio’s defense. Not only are Şengün All-NBA predictions looking strong early, but, so far, the work of the Rockets’ new shooting coach appears to be paying dividends as well.
Thompson and Şengün Are Shooting Threes

Shooting coach Chris Engelland worked extensively with Thompson and Şengün on their shooting this offseason. Either of them becoming non-liabilities from deep would be a legitimately era-defining development for the Rockets.
Well, in the win versus the Spurs, Şengün shot 2-of-4 from three, including scoring the first three points of the game. He shot 2-of-2 against the Mavericks as well.
Şengün started strong from three in 2025-26 before petering out. One encouraging difference this time around is that Thompson is also already 2-for-4 from three on the season.

The low volume makes the numbers themselves mean very little, but it’s likely a point of emphasis for neither player to force three-pointers. The shot is never going to be what their game is built around, but if they have the confidence to shoot them when wide open, defenses will have to reconsider their approach to Houston’s offense.

Add to the good news that Jabari Smith Jr. dropped a near-career-high 30 points in the Rockets opener, VanVleet grabbing at his leg during Friday night’s game turned out to be nothing, and Kevin Durant at 38 predictably still looks like Kevin Durant at 37.
The Last Word

The Rockets will play again on Saturday night versus the Atlanta Hawks in their first back-to-back of the season. Hopefully the team will take the cautious approach and rest returning players like VanVleet and Steven Adams . If Reed Sheppard can return from his previously day-to-day listed knee injury, even better. Busy in the midst of a back-to-back, the Rockets are back in business as a possible contender for the NBA title.

articles.headline: Police fire tear gas, arrest dozens as France braces for more protests
keyFacts: French officials said police arrested 135 people and fired tear gas during nationwide protests over living costs.
Security forces deployed up to 70,000 officers nationwide as thousands demonstrated against political leaders and economic conditions.
Yellow Vest organizers called for a new round of nationwide protests on October 31.
body: French police have arrested dozens and fired tear gas at some protestors Saturday as authorities stepped up security in major cities, aiming to prevent a repeat of . The nationwide demonstrations are focused on the high cost of living, and a massive turnout is expected again after more than half a million last week.

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 135 people have been arrested and a variety of weapons have been seized. The items confiscated include metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said. Nuñez added that, so far, "there has been no major incident" in the country.
Nuñez previously said as many as 70,000 officers will be deployed nationwide, along with helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons.

Demonstrations had been banned in the southeast city of Lyon, but about 150 protesters near the city's center briefly tried to block a road. Police fired tear gas to disperse the group. A 21-year-old student, who spoke to the Agence France-Presse on the condition of anonymity, described authorities as "really mobile."

"They come and disperse marches before they even form," the student said. A police helicopter was seen flying over the city, and security forces, armored vehicles and riot police vans were patrolling.

In Orleans, thousands of people marched against a congress held by Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally party. Le Pen is launching her campaign to succeed Emmanuel Macron as France's president. Elections will be held in six months, and surveys show Le Pen is best-placed to win. Demonstrators in Orleans protested both Macron and Le Pen.

"Macron resign. Le Pen in prison," the crowd yelled, according to the AFP. Police put their numbers at 11,000, while organizers said 26,000 took part. About 50 organizations, including labor unions, left-wing parties and student groups, had called for a protest against Le Pen's nationalist, anti-immigration party.
French media reported that the protest against the congress ended peacefully early Saturday afternoon. The gathering is expected to continue through Sunday.
Situation in Paris remains "calm"

Authorities described the atmosphere in Paris as "calm" as hundreds gathered at the Porte d'Italie for the city's only authorized march. The gathering was set to be held at the Bastille, in the city's center, but police ordered it moved to the more remote location on Paris' southeastern rim at the last minute.

Union organizers said they reluctantly agreed to the change. But union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters that it was "scandalous" that Macron had forbidden protestors from demonstrating "where we wish to demonstrate."
"We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be," she added.
A student named Lucas told CBS Saturday Morning that he believed it was "normal for people to be angry."
"There's like an escalation because people, we think that the government is not listening," Lucas said.

Throughout Paris, major museums are closed and many businesses have been boarded up. Art Basel, one of the world's most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday, but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organizers to cancel the weekend program.

The first-ever NFL game in France between the New Orleans Saints and remains scheduled for Paris on Sunday, but some associated venues have been shuttered. A pop-up NFL shop and where the Super Bowl trophy is on display and community sessions and events were scheduled, were closed Saturday. A similar venue for the New Orleans Saints was also postponed until Sunday. Another NFL pop-up shop remains open in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, the league said. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said earlier this week that preparations for the game had been made in consultation with U.S. and French authorities.
A soccer game scheduled to be held in Paris on Sunday, between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais, has been postponed until Monday night.

Parisian shopkeepers have been barricading their stores all week. Near Place de la République in Paris, one of last weekend's hot spots, a bank branch and other businesses were boarded up with wooden panels to deter potential looters.

Some 3,000 shops across France were damaged or looted last weekend. The demonstrations first erupted last month when high school students in the southeast of Paris protested for better conditions, but as people took to the streets to demand relief from rising living costs.
Organizers call for Halloween demonstrations

One group of protesters, the Yellow Vests, said they would hold another round of protests on Oct. 31. The Yellow Vests emerged about eight years ago as a loosely organized group that staged disruptive protests against Macron.

Organizers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the "authoritarian drift" of Macron's government and urging citizens to stand up for "public freedoms."

articles.headline: Paula Moltzan earns long-awaited first Alpine skiing World Cup win to open season
keyFacts: American Paula Moltzan won her first Alpine skiing World Cup in the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden, Austria.
Moltzan rallied from fifth place after the opening run to beat Lara Colturi by one hundredth of a second.
The 32-year-old became the oldest woman to earn her first World Cup victory after debuting in 2012.
body: American Paula Moltzan earned her first Alpine skiing World Cup win after more than a decade since she started racing on the sport's highest level.

Moltzan, 32, won the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden, Austria, rallying from fifth place after the opening run to win by one hundredth of a second over Albanian Lara Colturi combining times from two runs.
"It feels like a fairytale right now, pretty unreal," Moltzan said.
Moltzan, who debuted on the World Cup in 2012 and was dropped from the U.S. Ski Team ten years ago , had 10 second- or third-place finishes on the World Cup before Saturday.
ALPINE SKIING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule

After winning her first Olympic medal last February (bronze in the team combined), Moltzan changed skis, becoming the lone woman on the World Cup to sign with Van Deer, the outfit founded by eight-time World Cup overall champion Marcel Hirscher.
It paid off. She's the oldest woman to win her first World Cup.
Mikaela Shiffrin had the fastest opening run by 14 hundredths of a second over Swede Sara Hector, then was 27th-fastest in the second run to drop to seventh overall.
The men race a giant slalom in Soelden on Sunday at 5 a.m. and 8 a.m. ET, live on Peacock , which streams every race this season.

articles.headline: College football picks: Predictions against the spread, odds, betting lines for top 25 games in Week 8
keyFacts: Week 8 features two matchups between ranked college football teams, with both games involving Texas schools.
No. 19 Texas hosts No. 7 Ole Miss as the Longhorns try to recover from consecutive losses under quarterback Arch Manning.
No. 14 Houston travels to play No. 10 Utah in a matchup carrying Big 12 championship and College Football Playoff implications.
body: It's a big Texas weekend. There are only two ranked games featuring top-25 teams in Week 8, and each involves a Texas school.

No. 7 Ole Miss travels to No. 19 Texas (7:30 p.m. ET) in what feels like a referendum game for both Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian and starting quarterback Arch Manning. The narratives have gone into overdrive this week as Texas has lost its last two games, both to unranked opponents, as the Manning-led Texas offense has struggled mightily. To get back on track, Arch will have to beat the program that means so much to his family. Arch's father (Cooper), uncle (Eli) and grandfather (Archie) all played football at Ole Miss.

Later in the night, No. 14 Houston takes on No. 10 Utah in a game that has both Big 12 championship and College Football Playoff implications. The Utes didn't look great in a win against Colorado last week but remain one of the five last unbeaten Power Four teams. Houston's lone loss is a two-point defeat to Texas Tech, and the Cougars could take a big step toward being a CFP contender with a road win over Utah.

Other intriguing games include No. 6 Indiana at Michigan, No. 18 LSU at Auburn and No. 11 Tennessee at South Carolina. The Hoosiers are coming off a tough loss to Ohio State, while the Wolverines may have found something with true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr. In the battle of the Tigers, LSU will need a win to keep its playoff hopes alive. Tennessee catapulted itself up the SEC hierarchy with a win over Alabama last weekend and yet still is a 2.5-point underdog to the Gamecocks.
After a historic weekend that saw five top eight-ranked teams go down on a single day, the Week 8 slate isn't quite as promising, but there's plenty to get excited about.
Michigan vs. No. 6 Indiana

12 p.m. on Fox, Fubo (try free): We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP, and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. Pick: Under 41.5 -- Robby Kalland
No. 18 LSU vs. Auburn

12 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try free): What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Byrum Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits. Pick: LSU -9.5 -- Austin Nivison
No. 9 UCLA vs. Michigan State

3:30 p.m. on CBS CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App Paramount+ Premium: Michigan State has allowed only one team this season to average more than 4 yards per carry. The Spartans are capable of slowing down the Bruins' rushing attack, which is already trending in the wrong direction. It's hard to imagine the Spartans scoring enough to win the game outright against UCLA's stout defense. But a two-touchdown spread is a lot to cover for a Bruins team playing with its backup quarterback. Look for a low-scoring game won by UCLA's defense. Pick: Michigan State +14 -- David Cobb
No. 13 Alabama vs. Texas A&M

3:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try free): The Crimson Tide might be running on fumes here, playing their eighth game in eight weeks, especially considering the physical toll that comes with facing teams like Georgia and Tennessee. And while Texas A&M may be well off pace from preseason expectations and suffering from underwhelming performance, the Aggies are still a team with athletes and SEC-caliber bodies. A properly motivated Texas A&M team can make life a little bit harder for Alabama, even with the advantages they have on paper. For that reason, I could see this game being a little bit lower-scoring, with points tough to manufacture in what is ultimately an Alabama win. Pick: Under 50.5 -- Chip Patterson
No. 16 USC vs. Wisconsin

7:30 p.m. on NBC, Fubo (try free): Wisconsin is probably looking at the weather forecast for this game and wondering what it did to offend the weather gods. If there was any time to wish for temperatures in the 40s with biting wind, it's when USC is coming to town. Instead, the forecast is calling for temperatures in the 60s with a manageable breeze. Still, even if the weather won't have an oversized impact, I like the under here. USC may have won its two road trips so far this season, but the offense didn't look great against Penn State, and this Wisconsin defense is good. I also don't have much faith in the Wisconsin offense. Pick: Under 50.5 -- Tom Fornelli
No. 9 Ole Miss vs. No. 18 Texas

7:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try free): Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents.

But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight.

Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. Pick: Ole Miss +2.5 -- Brandon Marcello
No. 14 Houston vs. No. 10 Utah

10:15 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try free): Utah has been a dominant force over the first couple of weeks and will ultimately come away with a dramatic win in Salt Lake City. At the same time, Houston has been perhaps the most undervalued team nationally, rolling on both sides of the ball behind tremendous quarterback play from Conner Weigman. A nearly touchdown line is disrespectful to the machine Willie Fritz has built at Houston; don't be surprised if they pull the upset. Pick: Houston +6.5 -- Shehan Jeyarajah

articles.headline: NFL fumbles are climbing, and defenses are giving Peanut Tillman’s punch a bigger role
keyFacts: NFL fumbles reached 235 through the first six weeks of the 2026 season, representing a 28 percent increase from the previous year according to Elias Sports Bureau data.
Defenders are increasingly using the Peanut Punch technique, where players strike at the football with a closed fist to force it free.
The rise in fumbles has created coaching challenges for both defenses seeking turnovers and offenses focusing on ball security.
body: The ball is getting punched loose more often in the NFL, and the trend has made one old defensive technique feel new again.

Through the first six weeks of the 2026 season, the league had recorded 235 fumbles, up 28 percent from the same point a year ago, according to Elias Sports Bureau data reported by the New York Post. That increase has brought extra attention to the “Peanut Punch,” the technique popularized by former NFL cornerback Charles Tillman: defenders strike at the football with a closed fist to force it free.
Simplifying the idea

The idea is simple. Tackling ends the play; punching at the ball can end the drive. But turning the move into a reliable part of a defense takes practice, timing and control. The NFL has sent teams video examples of legal punches as well as examples that can draw an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

🤯 𝐖𝐎𝐖: NFL players have already fumbled the football 235 TIMES through the first six weeks of 2026. That's a 28% INCREASE from last season. Defenders are increasingly using the famous "Peanut Punch" technique to knock the ball loose. https://t.co/LJXOwx559t
— Polymarket Football (@PolymarketBlitz) October 23, 2026

That creates a coaching challenge on both sides of the ball. Defenses want players to attack the ball when the opportunity is there. Offenses have to make sure ball carriers protect it through contact, especially when defenders are targeting the ball instead of wrapping up. Coaches have described ball security as a priority, with some teams giving it more practice time.
Where it started

Tillman’s legacy is visible in that shift. His nickname became attached to a play that defensive coaches now teach across the league, years after he built a reputation for forcing fumbles in Chicago. The technique’s spread reflects the NFL’s constant search for turnovers, where even a small change in how a defender approaches a tackle can swing possession.

The numbers do not prove that the Peanut Punch alone caused the increase. Fumbles can rise for many reasons, including game situations and individual mistakes. But the league’s emphasis on teaching the technique shows how seriously teams are taking the opportunity to create turnovers—and how much more urgently offenses must protect the ball.

articles.headline: Lee Chang Dong ponders the ethics of the camera
keyFacts: Director Lee Chang Dong's seventh feature film, Possible Love, is inspired by a 2009 mass layoff at a Korean conglomerate and subsequent suicides.
The film explores labor struggles, human connection, and the ethical dilemmas and power dynamics involved in capturing other people's pain on film.
Possible Love was released in select United States theaters on October 23rd and will be available globally on Netflix on November 6th.
body: Lee Chang Dong’s seventh feature film, Possible Love, is inspired by true events from 2009, when a Korean conglomerate fired a third of its staff – 2,600 employees – after which many died by suicide. Possible Love is the latest in a long line of Lee movies that engage with themes of class or labor or religion or compressed modernity, that uniquely Korean affliction, without feeling didactic.
Lee Chang Dong ponders the ethics of the camera
In Possible Love, the director of Burning tackles labor struggle, human connection, and the nature of capturing others on film.

A different kind of movie would have captured the heat of that labor struggle. Possible Love picks up with the characters in the aftermath, a murkier time that defies easy understanding. The film opens with an epigraph: “Thou shall not covet.” What follows is a movie about characters who covet. They covet each other’s job, designer clothes, spouses, and positionality. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-Yeon) is the long-suffering wife of Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), her laid-off husband. At a funeral of a colleague who died by suicide, Mi-ok and Ho-seok meet another couple, documentary filmmaker Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) and her rich husband, Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). And off we go.

The Verge spoke with Lee during his trip to New York about how he arrived at his politics, porousness between people, the properties of the camera, and what it is like to work with Netflix. The interview was conducted in Korean and translated into English.
I am also from Daegu. I wonder how this fact shaped you? And more broadly, to whom or what do you owe your political education?

As you know well, Daegu is referred to as the heartland of conservatism in Korea. I went to school there, all the way through university, so I grew up steeped in that conservative disposition and was influenced by it. But until I graduated from college, in the spring of 1980, I didn’t realize how politically conservative Daegu citizens were.

That spring, in May of 1980, I participated in protests against the Chun Doo-hwan regime as a university student. It was on the streets that I met them, the citizens, and experienced their hardline sentiments in a visceral way. It was shocking to me. Afterwards, I thought a lot about how come the people in Daegu were so politically conservative. In light of all that, the thoughts of a person I perceive as myself, that person’s attitude towards the world, could only be bound with a certain kind of tension.

I was interested in how different directors respond to similar social forces in different ways – like Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite and Park Chan Wook’s No Other Choice. I imagine you know them both personally. What is the conversation between you all when working on your various projects?

We do know each other personally, but we seldom talk about our work. It might be the result of coincidence. Though of course, there might be a certain inevitability hidden within them. We lived through the same modern Korean history, and you cannot call that coincidence.

One thing does come to mind. A long time ago, I think before he made Mother, Bong Joon Ho told me over drinks that he had almost finished writing a script and wanted to show it to me. It was a story about a mother, and he was wrestling with how he could portray that person’s pain, whether he even had the right to. He said he wanted to show me the script. But once he sobered up, maybe he forgot, because he never showed it to me. Later, when I saw the film, I felt I might understand what he had been talking about.

Possible Love is concerned with similar questions: How can I portray another person’s story, another person’s pain? What position am I in? How much distance should I keep from them? You could say that these questions around the ethics of the camera are connected to the worry Bong Joon Ho had back then.

Like Ye-ji, I come from the so-called margins, and now report on that terrain, which is perhaps why watching her character pursue a near-vampiric level of access, I felt something close to repulsion. How were you able to represent the filmmaker–participant dynamic so accurately?

I can’t say how accurate it is. I don’t think Ye-ji’s attitude can be generalized. Not every documentary filmmaker has a rich husband. Nevertheless you can say Ye-Ji captures something universal about filmmakers, or those who deal in other people’s stories, directors such as myself, or reporters, in that they aren’t exactly the people they portray. Even if they came from a lower class, they are no longer of it. Their position in life has changed. And yet, in order to do their work, what do they do? When someone else’s suffering unfolds dramatically in front of them, are they to capture the moment on tape, or should they step away from the camera? Or maybe it isn’t unfolding dramatically in front of them, in which case, do they create a certain effect by producing the moment, by staging it?
I think those are basically properties of the camera. The moment you hold a camera you have power, and the camera operates according to that power.
It’s not so much that I portrayed it so precisely, but these properties of the camera are something worth thinking through together.

For us filmmakers, we don’t belong to the world of our subjects, nor are we on the side of capital either. We are in the middle where we are, it can be said, in a neutral, or perhaps cowardly position. Despite that, those who make movies, those who tell stories of others, in the end, can, through their efforts, bring about some small change.
In this film, Ho-seok ends up pouring out what’s inside of him in front of the camera, which functions as a kind of treatment, even if that isn’t what Ye-ji intended.
Possible Love is a collaboration between you and screenwriter Oh Jung-mi. How did you two come to work together, and what does that collaboration look like?

She is a student I met at Korea National University of Arts. You could say it’s a school that draws the most talented and ambitious students, and she was special even among them. By special I mean she was creative and wrote well, of course, but she also has a perspective, and the ability to take a step back and regard something, and find meaning in things.
As I get older, I grow duller and numb, and set in my ways, and she is a friend who reliably jolts me out of it, which is very precious to me.
I think I’m lucky. Not just with Oh Jung-mi but everyone around me that I work with is very precious to me, and I feel lucky to have met them.

The problem with Oh Jung-mi, though, is that while working together, I kept scrapping projects. So she suffered. But she never left. She stayed beside me, and even though she herself is someone who makes and develops films, she has given me a lot of help up to now.

Ye-ji documents in service of higher purpose. Mi-ok’s character snaps photos of the table spread for no purpose at all. The footage from the helicopter captures a moment of police brutality. How does the function of cinema compare to all the other instances in which we hit record?

Ye-ji has a desire to capture in her camera vanishing laborers [and] the value of their labor — not unlike her dry cleaner father. And yet, it is undeniable that she also regards their lives as source material for her own movie. As narrative filmmakers, stories of others in pain often is nothing but material for a commercial movie.

As for Mi-ok, she knows about the properties of the camera, but she, too, has a desire: to broadcast her pain, and her problems. She has a secondary desire, which is that she wonders if her husband’s traumas may not be healed through the camera, because she believes that his biggest issue is keeping all his problems, his despair and his anger, hidden.
So each has their own desires regarding the camera.

As a filmmaker, firstly, I had the goal of conveying the contents of the documentary Ye-ji was making, of capturing the sufferings of the laid-off laborers. I believed what Ye-ji tried to show, I had to show through my own film.

The group therapy session scene, for example, could be very long and tedious, and for some viewers it might be something that they cannot emotionally relate to, because they came to see a narrative film, not documentary. Despite that, I felt I had to convey it.

Regarding the crackdown scene, some of it appears through archival footage shot from a distance. But as someone making a fiction film, I also have a responsibility to convey Ho-seok’s subjective memory cinematically. So you could say within the narrative structure of Ye-ji’s documentary, multiple layers of roles and goals co-exist.
What are some notes you received from your American movie executives that felt unique to working in the American system versus Korean?

I didn’t feel that at all. From pre-production through post-production, Netflix, as the investor, never once interfered or offered unsolicited notes. Of course, I can’t generalize from that. I haven’t asked everyone else. But I had none of that. In that sense they absolutely guaranteed my independence and freedom as a director.
Now the film is finished and we are promoting it, and in particular part of what we call the Oscar campaign. I probably wouldn’t have gotten this kind of help without Netflix, that’s clear.
Possible Love was released in select US theaters October 23rd and will be available on Netflix globally on November 6th.

articles.headline: How long is too long for an HDMI cable?
keyFacts: HDMI Licensing Administrator does not specify an official maximum length, meaning distance depends on the cable, signal, and hardware.
Higher-bandwidth signals like 4K at 120Hz make long cable runs less forgiving, leading to sudden glitches rather than gradual picture degradation.
Active or optical cables can extend distance beyond passive copper limits, but many require specific source and display orientation.
body: How long is too long for an HDMI cable?
There’s no official maximum length, but higher-bandwidth signals can make long HDMI runs much less forgiving.

HDMI is wonderfully boring, which is refreshing in a tech world where so much is complicated. A 6-foot cable that connects a streaming box to a TV will likely fulfill its purpose for the duration of its life. Run one across a room, through a wall or up to a ceiling-mounted projector, however, and it gets a little less predictable.

There isn't an official maximum HDMI cable length. HDMI Licensing Administrator does not specify one, as the distance is dependent on the cable, the signal it's sending and the hardware at either end. Those 10-, 25- and 50-foot limits you see online are thus more like guidelines than set limits.
Bandwidth is a major factor. An old DVD player doesn't demand much from a cable, while 4K at 120Hz with HDR and VRR is a much heavier task. The longer the run, the less room there is for error.
Faster HDMI signals make long cable runs trickier

Passive HDMI cables transmit an electrical signal through copper, which weakens along the way. There is no universal distance limit, but longer runs become harder to maintain as bandwidth increases. This is why a cable that works fine at 1080p may not reliably handle 4K/120 at the same length.

There isn't a brick wall where passive HDMI suddenly stops working, either. One 25-foot cable can perform flawlessly while another may begin to act up sooner. A cable that supports 4K/60 can also fail when you switch to 4K/120.

The type of cable is important as well. Premium High Speed cables (HDMI 2.0) are certified for up to 18Gbps, while Ultra High Speed models (HDMI 2.1) support up to 48Gbps for applications such as 4K/120 gaming. The newer Ultra96 category (HDMI 2.2) raises that ceiling to 96Gbps for application that need the extra bandwidth. More bandwidth doesn't magically make a cable better at long distances; in fact, it's quite the opposite. The more information a cable is carrying, the shorter the effective distance.

When an HDMI cable reaches its limit, picture quality typically doesn't degrade gradually like an old analog TV, with the image becoming a little worse as the run gets longer. Instead, flickering, sparkling pixels, audio glitches, temporary black screens or no picture at all are more likely to occur. HDMI tends to go from "everything's fine" to "why is my TV doing that?" quickly.
Long HDMI runs may need active or optical cables

If a passive copper cable becomes unreliable, active copper is the next step. These cables use electronics to compensate for signal loss. Active optical HDMI converts the high-speed signal to light and can run well over 100 feet in some applications.

However, there's a simple mistake you can make with these. Unlike standard cables, many active and optical HDMI cables are directional, meaning one end is for the source and the other is for the display. If you plug one in backwards, you may get a black screen even though you have a good cable. That's a frustrating find after you've already routed it through a wall.

Home theater users have also reported long cables that look great until higher-bandwidth modes are activated, so complete testing is crucial. Don't stop after seeing your console's home screen. Before installing the cable permanently, test the highest resolution, refresh rate, HDR and VRR combination that you plan to use.

The remainder of the signal chain is important as well. Wall plates, extension tools like couplers, and any switches or AV receivers are other potential points of failure, so a direct source-to-display connection is a good place to start troubleshooting. Conduit and a pull string should also be considered for an in-wall run. HDMI standards change; drywall is much less enthusiastic about upgrades.

The most basic buying guideline is the least glamorous: buy the shortest cable that will reach comfortably, determine which cable category your equipment needs and look for the certification label rather than paying extra for vague "premium" claims.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed parlayed his race-obsessed medical research to fast-track, fund journey to Congress: critics
keyFacts: Critics and a Post review reported that Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed used race-focused medical research to advance his career.
El-Sayed received a $90,000 Soros fellowship in 2012 to pursue a PhD in epidemiology, according to the report.
Critics labeled El-Sayed's research as pseudoscience, and his campaign did not respond to requests for comment.
body: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed turned his weird science into a stepping stone, exploiting identity politics in academia to fast-track and fund his journey to Congress, according to critics and a Post review of his research.
A 2011 study, for example, suggested white people could take a lesson from Muslims who have lower suicide rates — thanks to Sharia law.
The study, titled “Suicide among Arab Americans” and funded in part with National Institutes of Health grants, looked at suicide deaths in Michigan between 1990 and 2007.
The research, published in the Public Library of Science journal, found that Arab men had roughly half the suicide rate of white men, while Arab women had a rate 24% lower than white women.

“According to traditional interpretations of Islamic Sharia law, suicide is considered haram or forbidden, and families of suicide victims can face ostracism within the Muslim community,” El-Sayed boasted in the paper’s conclusion.

Some of his race-obsessed studies include “Birth outcomes among Arab Americans in Michigan before and after the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001,” in 2008; and “Ethnic Inequalities in Mortality: The Case of Arab Americans” in 2011.

Others tackled “Racial and insurance-based disparities in the treatment of carotid artery stenosis: A study of the Nationwide Inpatient Sample” in 2015 and “The Color of Debt: Racial Disparities in Anticipated Medical Student Debt in the United States” in 2013.

“Our findings suggest that interethnic mating may be associated with increased risk for adverse birth outcomes among Arab ethnicity mothers,” he wrote at the time, back then going by the name Abdulrahman M. El-Sayed.
Critics panned the paper as pseudoscience.
“This is ‘science’ with “a pre-ordained racist & eugenics outcome,” Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Tx.) wrote on X. “Scary stuff.”
But his research at the time apparently got the attention of the family of far-left billionaire and Democratic mega-donor George Soros — which stepped in to bankroll his rising career.
In 2012, El-Sayed received the $90,000 Paul and Daisy Soros Fellowship for New Americans to pursue a PhD in epidemiology at Columbia University.
He graduated in 2014 and became executive director of the Detroit Health Department in 2015.
That information comes courtesy of Jeffrey Soros, the Hollywood producer nephew of the family patriarch, who hosted El-Sayed at his home in September for a celebrity-filled fundraiser in Los Angeles.

“I just wanted to welcome you here and express my appreciation for coming. And it’s been a privilege,” said Jeff Soros while standing alongside El-Sayed, according to video of his remarks obtained by Fox News Digital.
“Speaking of privilege, I’ve had the pleasure of knowing Abdul since 2012. I got to interview him as a finalist for my parents. Fellowship, the Paul and Daisy Soros Fellowship for New Americans.”

“We already knew he was a bigot, but this is over the top,” said Julian Epstein, former chief counsel for the Democratic House Judiciary Committee. “In the same way he used his antisemitic hate to try to win the primary, now we see he’s used his half-baked pseudo intellectual eugenics science to fatten out what looks like a pretty thin research record and perhaps persuade his more radical supporters that is really down with racial separatism.”
He added: “How much more evidence do moderate Democrats need in order to switch.”

Kyle Shideler, director of Homeland Security and Counterterrorism at the Center for Security Policy, previously told The Post the brotherhood’s goal is to “prevent Muslim Americans from assimilating into American culture” — a recurring theme that emerges throughout El Sayed’s research.

“The brotherhood wants to use political power in the United States to support activities abroad,” said Shideler. “At the end of the day, its big picture goal is to impose Islamic law on all nations everywhere and establish a caliphate.”
El Sayed’s campaign did not return The Post’s request for comment.

articles.headline: Aston Villa v Manchester City: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Nicolas Jackson scored an early goal to give Aston Villa the lead against Manchester City in the Premier League match.
Erling Haaland later brought Manchester City level with a downward header from six yards following a cross by Iliman Ndiaye.
Aston Villa came into the match after winning five of their previous six games despite a significant summer squad rebuild under manager Unai Emery.
body: 56 min: Good save by Suzuki! Doku cuts inside from the left and fires an angled pass into the underlapping Gvardiol. He takes the ball in his stride like a No10 and whacks a rising drive that is pushed over well by Suzuki.
55 min Now Cash is booked for a poor – possibly accidental – tackle on Doku. His studs went into the back of Doku’s foot, probably just below the achilles.

A clinical finish from Erling Haaland brings City level. Ndiaye, who has been excellent on the right, beat Manzanbi with a stepover and clipped an inviting cross to the far post. Haaland got up early, ahead of Lindelof, and slammed a downward header into the net from six yards.

50 min A promising City attack ends when Anderson overhits a cross from the De Bruyne Zone. He normally measures his crosses expertly from that position. On this occasion, the ball flies out of play and the home fans whistle with disdain.
47 min Villa break after an errant pass from Lewis. Eventually Maatsen pings a shot that ricochets behind for a corner. Cash takes, Haaland wins it in the air and City eventually clear.

A raw, compelling first half at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson’s early goal capped a ferocious start from Villa – who had more than 90% of the possession at that stage – and set up a fascinating clash of styles.

City dominated the ball for the rest of the half: the impressive Iliman Ndiaye hit the post and was one of two City players to have penalty appeals turned down. But Villa, with Jackson and John McGinn outstanding, were a constant menace in transition.
45 min One minute of added time. Cherki’s curving pass towards Haaland is cut out by the last defender Lindelof. There was a lot of grass behind Lindelof but Cherki didn’t quite get the pass right.
42 min Pound for pound, Unai Emery is the best manager in the world: discuss.

(I don’t know whether I think this, but it’s surely up for discussion. It’s astonishing that he has them playing this well so soon after losing Martinez, Konsa, Digne, Rogers, Tielemans, Rogers, Watkins.)

Alysson moves elegantly into the area from the right, hugging the ball on his left foot. He zig-zags between Dias and another City player and is about to shoot – probably score – when Dias makes a fabulous recovery tackle.

32 min Guehi is booked for fouling Jackson just outside the area. It was a bit of a wrestling match, and Guehi didn’t think he’d committed the foul. The home fans, by contrast, thought it should have been a Dogso red card. I’m pretty sure there was a covering defender.
With Villa seeing very little of the ball in the last 25 minutes, Nicolas Jackson has been fantastic.

31 min Now City want a penalty when Maatsen, who is really struggling, misses a lunging tackle at Ndiaye, who then goes over. Hard to tell whether he was fouled or whether he slipped. It was clumsy from Maatsen but it’s been cleared by VAR.

31 min “I’ve come late to the MBM and need to warn you not to put ideas into people’s heads,” writes Richard Hirst. “At the rate Man City are collecting points a 50 point deduction would be nowhere near enough to ensure that they finish below Fulham.”
30 min Manzanbi goes over in the area after running into Anderson. The Villa fans want a penalty but the referee isn’t interested; nor are VAR. It looked like Anderson just stood his ground.
29 min “Fantastic reading in the lee of Mt Ventoux that Villa have taken the lead,” writes Mike Daniels. “Nowhere to watch but thanks for the live report.”

Ndiaye been so sharp on the right. He cuts inside again, away from Maatsen, and sweps a left-foot curler across goal from the edge of the area. It beats the diving Suzuki, bounces up and hits the outside of the far post.

26 min A quick free-kick from McGinn, whose football brain is as big as his backside, leads to a corner that is punched away by Donnarumma. Terrific game, this - the clash of styles, the tempo, the slight edge that is going to lead to a shoving match any minute now.
24 min Another good run from Doku forces Villa into some desperate defending. They are simultaneously hanging on at 1-0, and threateningt to make it 2-0 whenever they break.
21 min Doku crackles past Alysson on the edge of the area and fires a low cross at Cherki. He sweeps a first-time shot towards goal and Suzuki falls on the ball to his left. Comfortable save.
Suzuki then belts the ball downfield and out for a throw-in in the City half. “If in doubt, ping one out,” says the TNT Sports commentator Darren Fletcher.

19 min Enzo Fernandez appeals for a penalty after a slight shove from Joao Gomes. Villa break, with Jackson all alone. He runs at a backpedalling defence before dragging a shot wide from the edge of the area.
VAR don’t intervene on the Fernandez incident. Gomes took a risk – both hands on the back – but I guess it falls under referee’s call.

13 min: Fine save by Suzuki! This is a cracking match. Ndiaye cuts inside from the right, beats two defenders and curls a fast left-foot shot towards the corner from 20 yards. Suzuki dives a long way to his right to push it away with both hands.

Dias’s risky crossfield pass was miscontrolled on the right by Guehi, allowing McGinn to push the ball into the penalty area for Jackson. He shuffled back inside Anderson, whose attempted tackle was a bit lazy, and lifted an emphatic sidefoot finish past Donnarumma. That was so cool from Jackson, who already has six goals for Villa.

6 min … which almost leads to a goal. McGinn took it short on the left, got it back and picked out the onrushing Alysson on the edge of the area. His fierce first-time shot was crucially blocked by Guehi.
4 min Villa work the ball nicely across the face of the City area before Cash’s cross is turned behind by Guehi. McGinn drives a long corner to Maatsen, whose sidefoot volley flies over the bar.

The players walk out of the tunnel, into the Birmingham rain. It doesn’t sound espeically hostile, although you can’t always tell on TV. The City fans are once again tooled up with inflatable bananas.

“Hi Rob,” writes Gary Naylor. “Barreling down the péage from Girona to Avignon, having spent the morning in the Dali Museum (still a third rater if you ask me), I have a moral dilemma. Can we ask Grok to direct us to a bar showing the Everton match? Or would that be shaking hands with both the AI and Musk devils? It was easier when you just had to wait until Monday afternoon and pick up a Guardian International for 50 francs.”

Heh. I remember reading Austria Vienna 5-1 Manchester United in the results section in August 1991. That was – and still is – the extent of my knowledge about the game. The papers didn’t cover the game, because it was still the cricket season.

Elliot Anderson has been chatting to TNT Sports. When asked whether he expected City to receive another hostile reception – this is their first away game since Anfield – he chuckled and said: “Yeah, probably. Everywhere we go, we’ll get it.”

It’s a huge, huge challenge today. They are a team who try to dominate, to impose their positioning, their skills and their tactical structure. We must be so intense in our focus and in our actions. Then, when we have the ball, we have try to threaten them. It’s a huge challenge, collectively and individually, against the best team in the league right now.

“There are no coincidences in life,” writes Krishnamoorthy V. “Your mention of The Shining in the preamble connects to The Overlook Hotel. Is it a reference to what the Premier League will do in its assessment of City’s appeal?”

Unai Emery and Enzo Maresca continue their policy of rotation, rotation, rotation. Matty Cash, Ian Maatsen, Boubacar Kamara and Johan Manzambi return to the Villa team in place of Tyrone Mings, Ibrahim Mbaye, Ross Barkley and Emi Buendia.

Phil Foden, who scored a hat-trick against AEK in the week, is back on the City bench. Marc Guehi, Iliman Ndiaye, Jeremy Doku and Erling Haaland come into the team; the other players to drop out are Rico Lewis, Allan and Floyd Samba.
Aston Villa (4-2-3-1) Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Joao Gomes; Alysson, Manzambi, McGinn; Jackson.

Bayern Munich say their head coach Vincent Kompany, who was taken to hospital after collapsing during training on Friday, will be absent for “weeks rather than days”. Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital.
You can read about that, and all the rest of the day’s fitba news, on our matchday live blog.

It was five months ago but it feels a lot longer. When these two sides met in May to finish the season, the contest doubled as Pep Guardiola’s leaving party after 10 years in the job and twice as many trophies, an era now laden with asterisks. It must be surreal for Aston Villa supporters, too. Their 2-1 victory at the Etihad Stadium, inspired by two goals from Ollie Watkins to complete a league double over City, came only four days after their Europa League triumph in Istanbul, where Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Emi Buendía were the scorers.

Buendía is the only one left in claret and blue as Unai Emery builds a new side, one that has picked up in form after a single point from their first four league games. City, meanwhile, are thriving on the pitch: victory would make them just the third side to win their first eight games of a Premier League season.
You remember Manchester City, don’t you? They made one or two headlines earlier in the month, but have since been kept off the back pages by a neighbouring circus.

Since the weird (and wonderful, if you’re a City fan) win at Anfield, Enzo Maresca’s team have played three games, all at home. They were undressed by PSG, held off Ipswich last weekend and hammered AEK on Tuesday. Oh, and Elliot Anderson made the James Bond shortlist.

City are top of the Premier League with a perfect record of seven wins from seven. But like life, The Shining and those dreams in which all your teeth fall out, nobody really knows what it means. City are on 21 points, but for all we know it could effectively be -29. Yes, I have just pulled that number from my fundament. No, I don’t have any inside knowledge.
The only thing the City players – who, lest we forget, had nowt to do with the 115 charges – can win football matches and see where it takes them.

Today’s will be tougher than most. Unai Emery has somehow squashed a year of transition into a month. Villa lost six of their Europa League-winning XI in the summer and started the season terribly. But they have won five of the last six games and are playing with a rhythm that belies the summer rebuild. On recent evidence, losing all those great players really was just a flesh wound.

articles.headline: The parties have flipped on support for Israel
keyFacts: During the 1976 presidential race, Democratic nominee Jimmy Carter ran to the right of Republican incumbent Gerald Ford on support for Israel.
Today, debate over U.S. policy toward Israel within the Democratic Party has shifted toward hostility, with several anti-Israel candidates winning primaries.
President Donald Trump has strongly supported Israel and endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, contrasting sharply with current Democratic divisions.
body: Much in American politics has changed over the past 50 years. Perhaps on no topic more than which party is more favorable or hostile to Israel .

In a move seemingly unrecognizable in today’s political climate, during the 1976 presidential race, Democratic nominee Jimmy Carter ran to the right on Israel against the Republican president he sought to oust from office, Gerald Ford . The issue likely helped Carter win narrowly over the GOP incumbent.

Now, on the Democratic side, debate over U.S. policy toward Israel is increasingly a game of how hostile to be. Or whether to even say the country should exist as a Jewish state. It’s an internecine debate that’s only grown more heated since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks killed more than 1,200 people in Israel, with 251 taken hostage. This spurred Israel’s attacks on Gaza , which has led to an estimated 70,000 Palestinians killed.

The anti-Israel cause motivated several Democratic congressional candidates in this year’s Democratic primaries. Among them, notably, were a pair of winning Democratic Socialists of America candidates in New York backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani: Claire Valdez in the 7th Congressional District, covering northern Brooklyn and western Queens, and Darializa Avila Chevalier in the 13th Congressional District, covering northern Manhattan and western Bronx.
President Gerald Ford speaks as Democratic nominee Jimmy Carter listens during a televised debate in Sept. 23, 1976, held at Philadelphia’s Walnut Street Theater. (AP Photo)

Mamdani also backed a one-time mayoral rival, Brad Lander, in the 10th Congressional District, covering Lower Manhattan and northwestern Brooklyn. Lander beat four-year Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY) in the primary. Lander, Valdez and Chevalier are set to enter Congress in January, as the Nov. 3 midterm general elections are only formalities in their deep-blue districts.

They’ll be joined in the House by a new swath of far-left Democratic primary winners set for November wins in districts overwhelmingly favoring their party: Melat Kiros in Colorado, Adam Hamawy in New Jersey and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania. These newcomers will be in office during the last two years of President Donald Trump’s second, nonconsecutive term.

Trump has called himself the “best president in the history of Israel.” His supporters cite large-scale joint military strikes against Iran initiated on Feb. 28. And they point to his first White House stint, in 2018, when the Trump administration recognized Jerusalem as Israel’s capital and moved the U.S. Embassy there from Tel Aviv, along with a 2019 presidential proclamation recognizing Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, which Israel captured from Syria in 1967.

Of course, Trump has sometimes clashed with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu . In June, after an Israeli strike in Beirut threatened a peace deal with Iran, Trump told Axios about the strikes in Lebanon , “Why did Bibi have to do a f***ing attack? I was so pissed off. I let him know. He has no f***ing judgment. I let him know that.”
Still, on Oct. 18, Trump endorsed Netanyahu, just nine days before Israel’s Oct. 27 elections.
Carter capitalized on strong bipartisan support for Israel

Today, opposition to Israel has emerged as a litmus test for some Democrats . But 50 years ago, the Democratic presidential nominee saw political opportunity in taking the opposite tack. Carter, who had been Georgia governor from 1971-75, called himself a far better friend of Israel than his Republican opponent, Ford.

Carter would eventually become a sharp critic of Israel, especially after leaving the White House. During a record nearly 45-year ex-presidency until his Dec. 29, 2024 death, Carter increasingly lashed out at the Jewish State, including the 1985 book The Blood of Abraham . Nearly 22 years later, he came out with another provocatively titled (to Israel supporters) successor book, Palestine: Peace Not Apartheid .

But back in 1976, Israel still enjoyed strong bipartisan support, and Carter was eager to win Jewish votes in key swing states like Florida and New York (yes, both were battleground states at the time). Amid protracted negotiations between Israel and Egypt over military disengagement in the Sinai Peninsula following the 1973 Yom Kippur War, a frustrated Ford warned Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin in 1975 that he was directing an immediate reassessment of U.S. policy in the Middle East, “including our relations with Israel.” Seventy-five senators pushed back on him.

In a May 1975 letter to Ford , the senators – including 50 Democrats – wrote that they expected the administration’s foreign aid request “will be responsive to Israel’s urgent military and economic needs.” They added that the history of the Arab-Israeli conflict “demonstrates that any Israeli withdrawal (from captured territories) must be accompanied by meaningful steps toward peace by its Arab neighbors.”

The following year, Carter went on a strikingly personal attack on Ford at their Oct. 6 debate, accusing him of showing “a weakness in yielding to pressure” from Arab countries. At the time, Israel didn’t have diplomatic relations with any of its Arab neighbors.

“The Arabs have put pressure on Mr. Ford, and he’s yielded, and has permitted a boycott by the Arab countries of American businesses who trade with Israel, or who have American Jews owning or taking part in the management of American companies,” Carter said.

Today, that debate is mostly remembered for Ford’s gaffe that there was “no Soviet domination of Eastern Europe.” But Carter also tried to capitalize on what he considered another foreign policy liability and claimed that military support for Israel had eroded under Ford.

“This is a deviation from idealism,” Carter said. “It’s a deviation from a commitment to our major ally in the Middle East, which is Israel. It’s a yielding to economic pressure on the part of the Arabs on the oil issue. And it’s also a tremendous indication that under the Ford administration we have not addressed the energy policy adequately.”
Two weeks later, at an event in Miami Beach, Carter vowed to end the Arab boycott.

“For the first time in the history of our nation, we have a president and an administration who are circumventing the Bill of Rights,” he shouted to an enthusiastic and predominantly Jewish audience, as the New York Times described it.

“It doesn’t matter in principle whether it’s Jews or Catholics or Baptists,” Carter said. “It’s a matter of morality. It’s got to be changed, and you have my word that it will be. We’ll get rid of the Arab boycott,” which he called “an insult and a disgrace.”

After Carter’s remarks, he made his way through hundreds of “nearly delirious” supporters, the Times reported, “shaking hands, groping through the screen of security agents around him, munching a chocolate pastry at a kosher bakery, chatting amiably with little old ladies and sampling the grapes at a produce market. South Miami Beach, a retirement haven for elderly Jews from all parts of the country, embraced Mr. Carter as though he were a member of the Knesset.”

After Carter beat Ford in a close election – carrying both New York and Florida – the new president signed an amendment to the Export Administration Act in 1977 which banned American companies from complying with some foreign boycott practices, such as secondary and tertiary boycotts targeting Israel. More significantly, he presided over the 1978 Camp David Accords , which led to a March 26, 1979 peace treaty between Israel and Egypt.

But his post-presidency was often marked by sharp criticism of Israeli policy. In his book, Palestine: Peace Not Apartheid , Carter included an incendiary line that Arabs and Palestinians should “make it clear that they will end the suicide bombings and other acts of terrorism when international laws and the ultimate goals” of a proposed peace accord “are accepted by Israel.”

At an appearance at Brandeis University in 2007 , Carter admitted that the sentence “was worded in a completely improper and stupid way,” and that he had asked the publisher to remove it. “I apologize to you personally, to everyone here,” he said.
That same year, 14 Jewish members of the Carter Center’s board of councilors resigned in protest over the book for blaming Israel for the lack of progress on a peace deal.
“We can no longer support your strident and uncompromising position,” they wrote in a letter to Carter . “This is not the Carter Center or the Jimmy Carter we came to respect and support.”
TRUMP BACKS NETANYAHU FOR REELECTION, SAYS ISRAELI PM CRITICAL ALLY AGAINST IRAN

Abe Foxman, the late director of the Anti-Defamation League, responded to the book by calling Carter a “bigot.” Deborah Lipstadt, who went on to become special envoy against antisemitism under President Joe Biden, wrote in a Washington Post opinion piece at the time that the book, “while exceptionally sensitive to Palestinian suffering, ignores a legacy of mistreatment, expulsion and murder committed against Jews. It trivializes the murder of Israelis.”
It’s a safe bet that in 2028, the Democratic candidate will not be eager to outflank the Trump administration when it comes to supporting Israel.

Frederic J. Frommer (@ffrommer) is a sports and politics historian who has written for the Washington Post , the New York Times , the Atlantic , and other national publications, and is working on a book on ’70s baseball.

articles.headline: QuestAway class tier list
keyFacts: QuestAway has launched its 1.0 version featuring six different character classes that are ranked into S, A, and B tiers.
The Healer and Mage are ranked in the S-tier because of their essential party healing and high damage output.
The Warrior, Assassin, and Engineer are placed in the A-tier, while the Archer is ranked in the B-tier due to weak defense.
body: QuestAway is now available in 1.0, and there are six different classes to pick from. Each of them perform different roles, and they have their respective strengths and weakness.
In this guide, I will assess all six classes and place them in different tiers.
Complete QuestAway class tier list
I have used three different tiers to rank the six available classes.
S-tier classes overpowered in the current build.
A-tier classes will require you to use the proper equipment pieces.
B-tier classes are underpowered in the current build of the game.
S-tier

Healer: Being the only healing class in the game, the Healer is important for any party. While I won’t necessarily begin as a Healer, you’ll need to add one. The class not only heals your party members, but it also offers shields to help them survive.

Mage: While the Mage isn’t the tankiest unit by any means, it makes up for it with insane damage. You have different elemental spells in the form of fire, lightning, ice, and arcane. All four of them do amazing damage as long as you get the proper build. The Mage is perhaps the best non-melee damage option you can have.
A-tier

Warrior: Mg only issue with the Warrior class is the amount of bleed damage it manages to deal. The damage is not low, but it could have been higher. I have tried going in with different builds, but nothing has worked so far. That said, this is the best build to start with for beginners, as you will get to learn the game without getting into complicated mechanics.

Assassin: This class does much more damage than Warrior, and the playstyle is also quite different. However, it doesn’t have the life and hit points that the Warrior offers. This class is also harder to master for beginner players, so it gets placed in this tier.

Engineer: Despite being classed as a ranged character, the Engineer is a very fun class. It’s unlike anything we typically see in this type of game. The Engineer relies entirely on her set of gadgets and different mechanisms to do the bulk of the damage. There is a bit of a learning curve, but once you get her build done, the Engineer can be a mighty option to have in your party.
B-tier

Archer: the Archer’s success depends on her build. She is one of the hardest characters to manoeuvre because she has extremely weak defense. You will need to pair her in a party with other classes that can complement and protect her.
The post QuestAway class tier list appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
keyFacts: Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara stated that Ukraine's connection to the Starlink satellite network is now stable and fully restored.
Kyiv previously accused US President Donald Trump of directing Elon Musk to limit Starlink connectivity, which Trump denied.
Khmarasaid the restored connection allows speeds exceeding 400km/h, which is crucial for front-line military operations and drone logistics.
body: - Published
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.
This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".
Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.
"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.
Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.
Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.
Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.
Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher.
While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war.
Zelensky said that, as well as seemingly limiting Starlink capability in Ukraine, the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump also denied.
Meanwhile, fighting on the ground continues.

Russia's ministry of defence wrote on Telegram on Saturday that their air defences shot down 616 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones, striking a number of regions across the country, including Russian-annexed Crimea.
Sergey Aksyonov, the region's Moscow-backed governor, said restrictions on electricity and water had been put in place because of power cuts caused by the drone strike.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities said they struck a missile component manufacturer, a chemical plant and an aircraft at a military airfield inside Russia in the past 24 hours.
They also said that Russia carried out 88 air strikes using 309 glide bombs and 10,270 kamikaze drones on Friday.

articles.headline: After 14 years of development, Factorio's final major update is out now
keyFacts: Developer Wube Software released update 2.1, which marks the final major patch and the end of 14 years of active development for Factorio.
The update focuses on quality-of-life features, polish, improved space logistics, and an overhaul to enemy Biter mechanics rather than new planets.
Wube stated that future plans include working on new prototypes, though the studio does not expect to share details for a long time.
body: The whistle has blown. The belts have stopped. The furnace is silent and cold. After 14 years of continual development, Factorio has received its final major update.

Developer Wube Software revealed that update 2.1 would be the last significant patch for its genre-defining factory building sim back in May, with the team deciding the game had "reached a good place to conclude active game development". The decision comes two years after Wube released Factorio's remarkable Space Age expansion, which lets players take their industrialisation efforts into the stars and across four wildly different alien planets.

If you were hoping Wube might sign off on Factorio on a similarly spectacular note, you may be disappointed. In its latest Friday Facts blog, the developer reiterates that 2.1 "isn't about new planets, enemies or research trees," and instead delivers "a big collection of quality of life, small features, polish, and the things we wanted to for 2.0 but didn't have time for."

This doesn't mean 2.1 has nothing of interest, however. Quite the opposite. The primary changes revolve around the space logistics introduced by Space Age, with Wube making it easier to ferry goods up into space and between planets. Rockets, for instance, can now carry multiple different items rather than just one thing, making it considerably easier to get space platforms built. On top of that, platforms can also transfer items between one another in orbit and automatically import items from all available locations.

Also on the space logistics front, Wube has added a constructable unloading bay that can be attached to landing pads, allowing inserters to pull out items and place them directly onto belts, into trains and so forth. This should make interplanetary logistics a bit easier.

There are also a bunch of non-Space Age related changes. Most interesting is an overhaul to the Biters that attack your base. Wube has altered the game so that biter expansion grouping scales with evolution, to ensure that clearing out biters poses a "meaningful challenge rather than lots of tiny annoying nests." Biters will also "choose more natural locations" to build new habitats and will expand their territory regardless of whether the player chooses to explore the map early.

Elsewhere, the update reintroduces fluid mixing prevention, makes some tweaks to Space Age's Quality system, and adds snazzy new graphics for assembling machines, oil refineries, rocket silos and heat exchangers. Finally, the patch adds a new rendering system that makes it easier for pumps to connect to rail fluid wagons. This might just be the thing I'm most excited about, because setting up fluid pumps is always an enormous faff.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While we may see some smaller patches in the future, 2.1 marks the definitive end of development for Factorio. As for what Wube's plan is going forward, the studio said it was working on some new prototypes back in May, but it stressed that "there will not be anything to share for a long time." For now, we'll just have to settle for playing one of the greatest games ever made.

Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims.
